clue.text: Found in flight before landing

parts.note: reads like an aircraft's approach, but a flight is also a run of steps that ends at a landing on a staircase

explanation.surface: Something discovered on an aeroplane just before it touches down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps in a house climbs up to a landing, the flat stretch between floors.

clue.text: It is not the common sort of pollution

parts.note: 'T is the clipped form of it, as in 'tis
ain't is the uneducated, common form of is not or isn't

explanation.surface: Some unusual kind of contamination is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the common sort of' tells you to use the vulgar contraction: 'T + AIN'T, i.e. it ain't, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or corruption spoiling something pure.

clue.text: That which is responsible for the current stoppage

definitions.text: That which is responsible for the current stoppage

parts.words: That which is responsible for the current stoppage
parts.note: sounds like whoever caused the present halt, but current is electric current, which this material blocks

explanation.surface: Someone is being blamed for the present strike or hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber, glass and similar non-conducting materials prevent electricity flowing where it should not.

clue.text: There's good reason for disorder in a sty

indicators.note: the letters are put in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A messy pigsty gives someone a fair excuse for their own untidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is a link to the definition at the start; 'for disorder' signals rearranging INASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of soundness of mind: being of good reason means being mentally sound.

clue.text: Material for a churchwarden

parts.note: looks like cloth for a parish officer, but a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe

explanation.surface: Fabric needed to dress a parish official.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden pipe is made of fine white clay of the kind used for tobacco pipes.

clue.text: Hope alone sustained him

parts.note: reads as a captive kept going only by optimism, but Hope is Anthony Hope, the novelist who alone created this character

explanation.surface: A captive in despair survived only on optimism.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope's 1894 adventure novel about Ruritania has this title character, sustained in print by his author alone.

clue.text: Subject of Dostoevsky's masterpiece

parts.note: Dostoevsky's masterpiece is Crime and Punishment, and crime and punishment is the field of study meant

explanation.surface: A literature question about what a great Russian novel is about.
explanation.definitionFit: This academic discipline studies punishment of criminals and prison management, crime and punishment in short.

clue.text: A form of distinction

definitions.meaning: a form is a school year group
style or excellence, as in a player with real quality

explanation.definitionFit: A school form is a group of pupils taught together; having elegance or high quality is also having this.

clue.text: One George was one such bookmaker

definitions.text: One George was one such bookmaker

parts.words: One George was one such bookmaker
parts.note: suggests a racecourse bookie named George, but a bookmaker here is one who makes books, and George Eliot was a woman writer

explanation.surface: A man called George took bets at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans) was a female novelist, the old word for a woman writer.

clue.text: The monopoly of disagreeable people ?

parts.note: disagreeable is read literally as given to disagreeing, so what such people have all to themselves is quarrelling

explanation.surface: Unpleasant people seem to have cornered some market.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord and strife are what those who disagree produce.

clue.text: He has this faculty with cards

definitions.text: He has this faculty with cards

parts.words: He has this faculty with cards
parts.note: faculty means a university department, as well as the knack of a skilled card player

explanation.surface: Someone is gifted at card games.
explanation.walkthrough: A faculty is a university division as well as a talent; a card sharp has arts (tricks) with cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A university faculty of humanities is named this, and tricks or skills are also called by the word.

clue.text: Titles to apply to one weapon

indicators.note: to apply the letters to a new use is to work them into a different order

explanation.surface: Honours are to be awarded to a single armament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apply' signals rearranging TITLESTO; 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim dagger with a narrow blade is a classic Italian weapon.

clue.text: Not so much gold as money he takes for his property

definitions.text: money he takes for his property

parts.note: less means not so much
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone prefers cash over gold in exchange for their land.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who lets property under a lease collects rent for it.

clue.text: This one can't complain of being followed

definitions.text: This one can't complain of being followed

parts.words: This one can't complain of being followed
parts.note: the one at the end of a line has nobody behind it, so cannot be followed

explanation.surface: Someone is free of a stalker.
explanation.definitionFit: The final item in a sequence has nothing coming after it.

clue.text: The object of dressing for a parade

definitions.text: The object of dressing for a parade

parts.words: The object of dressing for a parade
parts.note: dressing is the military term for lining troops up straight, not putting on uniform

explanation.surface: Why soldiers put on smart clothes before a march past.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks makes the soldiers stand in straight, even lines.

clue.text: Just too old to be sweet

definitions.text: Just too old to be sweet

parts.words: Just too old to be sweet
parts.note: alludes to the phrase sweet sixteen: an age a little beyond that is too old

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who has outgrown charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Two years past the proverbial sweet sixteen, the age of legal adulthood in Britain.

clue.text: You can feel it, by gum !

definitions.text: You can feel it, by gum !

parts.words: You can feel it, by gum !
parts.note: by gum is a mild Northern English oath, but gum is also the flesh round the teeth

explanation.surface: An excited Northerner insists something is palpable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in a molar or incisor is felt in the mouth, next to the gums.

clue.text: Gilbertian MP

parts.note: a character from a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta who ends up in Parliament

explanation.surface: An absurd member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In Iolanthe, by Gilbert and Sullivan, the Arcadian shepherd who is half a fairy is made a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-fairy shepherd of Iolanthe enters Parliament, so he is the operetta's MP.

clue.text: It may lay the foundation for a good score

definitions.text: It may lay the foundation for a good score

parts.words: It may lay the foundation for a good score
parts.note: score suggests a sporting total, but here it is a musical score, which is set to words

explanation.surface: Something that helps a batsman or team build a big total.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera is written first and the composer sets the music to it.

clue.text: Hop into it to dry out

definitions.text: Hop into it to dry out

parts.words: Hop into it to dry out
parts.note: sounds like jumping into somewhere to get dry, but hop is the plant, put into a kiln for drying

explanation.surface: Advice to jump in somewhere and get dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops, common in Kent, the hop-growing county of southern England.

clue.text: Criminals who are bent

definitions.meaning: as a verb, bends or curves, read as they are bent

explanation.definitionFit: Swindlers are called by this word, and to bend something is to curve it in the same word.

clue.text: To hostelry, dined — that's natural

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Going to a pub and eating there is the most normal thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' and 'that's' are links between the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inborn quality is natural rather than learned.

clue.text: March in front of it, always

definitions.text: March in front of it, always

parts.words: March in front of it, always
parts.note: march looks like an order to walk ahead, but March is the month that always precedes this one

explanation.surface: An order to keep marching at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the calendar follows March every year.

clue.text: Naughty time to begin an operation ?

definitions.text: Naughty time to begin an operation ?

parts.words: Naughty time to begin an operation ?
parts.note: naughty is read as nought-y, i.e. having a nought or zero in it

explanation.surface: A mischievous moment to launch a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment set for a military attack to start is the hour counted from nought.

clue.text: Pigment that may be burnt

parts.note: this brown earth colour comes raw or burnt, burnt meaning roasted to a darker shade

explanation.surface: A painter's colour at risk of catching fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural brown earth used in paints, sold as raw or roasted to a reddish brown.

clue.text: The thing for a close shave

definitions.text: The thing for a close shave

parts.words: The thing for a close shave
parts.note: close shave suggests a razor, but it means a narrow escape, called a thing of the same name

explanation.surface: A recommendation for the best razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is called a near thing, and near also means close.

clue.text: In these the men in control took back seats

definitions.text: In these the men in control took back seats

parts.words: In these the men in control took back seats
parts.note: suggests leaders stepping aside, but in these horse-drawn cabs the drivers sat high up behind the passengers

explanation.surface: Bosses who chose to step out of the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian two-wheeled horse-drawn carriages for hire had the driver's seat raised at the back.

clue.text: Apple-picker, a classic runner-up

parts.note: a figure from Greek myth who stopped mid-race to pick up golden apples and so came second

explanation.surface: An orchard worker who came second in a famous race.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the swift huntress lost a footrace to Hippomenes by stooping to gather golden apples he dropped.

clue.text: Guides useful to the Beefeaters ?

definitions.meaning: Beefeaters are Tower of London guards, but read literally as beef eaters, young bullocks are useful to them

explanation.definitionFit: To direct is this verb; young castrated bulls raised for beef are the noun.
